## Allocation and independent capability seams

Original `shaders.properties:193–219` guards all images with `VX_SUPPORT`.
HIGH selects `VOXEL_VOLUME_SIZE=192`. There are no 2D image declarations:

| Name / sampler | Target and dimensions | Internal / upload format / type | Clear each frame |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `voxel_img` / `voxelSampler` | 3D, 192 × 96 × 192 | R8UI / RED_INTEGER / UNSIGNED_INT | true |
| `floodfill_img` / `floodfillSampler` | same | RGBA16F / RGBA / HALF_FLOAT | false |
| `floodfill_img_copy` / `floodfillSamplerCopy` | same | RGBA16F / RGBA / HALF_FLOAT | false |

Exact [ShaderProperties bytecode](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r3/solas-original-mac-clear-prerequisite-r1/shaderpack.properties.ShaderProperties.javap.txt:1964)
maps nine tokens and relative=false to TEXTURE_3D. The boolean before relative
is the recurring-clear flag, not a request to omit initial clearing.
[GlImage](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r3/solas-original-mac-clear-prerequisite-r1/gl.image.GlImage.javap.txt:20)
allocates level 0 with a null data buffer, configures integer nearest or float
linear filters, clamp-to-edge and level/LOD limits 0, then unconditionally clears
the full level to zero. `IrisRenderingPipeline.beginLevelRendering` separately
calls the same GL clear for recurring-clear images. Fixing only setup would
leave the voxel recurring-clear failure.

Original `shadow.glsl:92–96,114,132` guards its `uimage3D`, image-store extension
and voxelization include with VX_SUPPORT. In contrast, all three native
`shadowcomp.csh` entries start with `#version 430 compatibility`; their included
`programs/shadowcomp.glsl:24,91,93` declares/writes 3D flood-fill images.
Those compute entry points require their native `program.*shadowcomp.enabled`
guard to disable them on Mac. A texture clear cannot supply compute or image
load/store support. Iris checks compute using the actual `glDispatchCompute`
pointer; CUSTOM_IMAGES capability uses `supportsImageLoadStore` rather than
the clear pointer. Those capabilities are separate, and their values on the
historical context remain unrecorded. Khronos defines these separate facilities
in [ARB_compute_shader](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/ARB/ARB_compute_shader.txt)
and [ARB_shader_image_load_store](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/ARB/ARB_shader_image_load_store.txt).

## Concrete native-guard mismatch to resolve

Original `common.glsl:842–844` defines VX_SUPPORT only when **not** MC_OS_MAC;
`common.glsl:2090` also undefines LPV_FOG without VX_SUPPORT. The earlier
[focused common preprocessing](solas-shader-lod-candidate-r1.md) confirms native
Mac VX exclusion. This is Solas's original Mac behavior, not an authorized
quality/preset reduction.

The exact pinned macro is **MC_OS_MAC**, not OS_MAC. `StandardMacros$1`
maps `Util.OS.OSX` to case 1; `getOsString()` case 1 returns MC_OS_MAC;
`createStandardEnvironmentDefines()` defines that returned name. The actual
Iris load path passes that list into `new ShaderPack`, and its GLSL preprocessing
uses the environment list. These are pinned binary call paths, beyond source
intent. With that normal OSX environment the original common guard excludes VX,
as the prior preprocessing confirms. A historical runtime macro dump was not
captured; this conclusion assumes normal `Util.getPlatform()` OSX classification,
consistent with the retained macOS log.

Pinned Iris `OptionAnnotatedSource` scans lines lexically and recognizes a bare
`#define VX_SUPPORT` as a true boolean option; it does not execute surrounding
GLSL conditionals during that scan. `PropertiesPreprocessor.getBooleanValues`
exports true option values as macros. `ShaderPack` evaluates native program
enable predicates through `BooleanParser.parse(expression, OptionValues)`,
not through common.glsl's executed macro state. The disassembled methods are
saved in the stage. This predicts that the native conditional definition can
become true in properties/program decisions even when false in Mac GLSL.
It explains the observed image-allocation seam, but **effective option values
and complete option merge behavior were not actually invoked/captured here**.
Do not present the inferred parser cause as an observed runtime diagnosis.

The one practical next experiment is a bounded **CPU-only pinned-Iris parser
reproduction**, before any client: load byte-identical Solas and native HIGH/+0
with the actual Mac standard macro environment; record discovered
VX_SUPPORT/default/effective value, preprocessed image declarations and all
three shadowcomp enable decisions. Expected native Mac result is no images and
disabled shadowcomp. If the inferred true value is reproduced, the changed
premise is a narrowly scoped loader correction that aligns this internal
capability flag in **both** properties and program predicates with Solas's
existing Mac guard, preserving shader bytes, native user options and HIGH.
A properties-only macro removal is insufficient because program predicates
still read OptionValues. The staged
[boundary sketch](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r3/solas-original-mac-clear-prerequisite-r1/prerequisite-sketch.txt)

## Clear-equivalence boundary and stopping decision

Khronos's [ARB_clear_texture specification](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/ARB/ARB_clear_texture.txt)
allows earlier upload or framebuffer-clearing approaches and specifies null
clear data as zeros. A zero upload could initialize the actual 3D level using
supported TexSubImage3D without changing formats; layer-by-layer framebuffer
clears would additionally need proved attachment completeness/renderability.
Neither operation establishes the voxel graph's compute/image capabilities.
No clear fallback code was staged because the requested 2D premise is false
and preserving an enabled voxel graph still leaves independent unsupported
premises. No new fallback buffers or GL4.3 bypass are staged. Parent/advisor
review precedes any integration or original launch.
